checklist: Open any project, or create one from the Third Person template. In the Content Drawer, choose FX, then Niagara System, then New system from selected emitters, and pick Simple Sprite Burst. Name the system FXS_RibbonTrail and drag it into a level.
In the Render group, delete the Sprite Renderer and add a Ribbon Renderer. Pick DefaultRibbonMaterial as its material. To find this material, turn on Show Engine Content and Show Plugin Content.
In the Emitter Update group, set the Life Cycle Mode of Emitter State to System. Then add a Spawn Rate module with a rate of about 100.
In the Particle Spawn group, set Lifetime, Color and Ribbon Width. Add a Shape Location module set to Ring / Disk and an Add Velocity module set to From Point, so that the ribbon spirals.
In the Particle Update group, remove Scale Color. Add an Acceleration Force module with a negative Z value so that the ribbon falls.
Try one setting of the Ribbon Renderer, either UV0 Tiling Distance or Tessellation, and note what changed.

Open any project, or create one from the Third Person template. Choose how Play In Editor (PIE) opens. Click the three dots next to the Play button in the main toolbar and pick New Editor Window (PIE) or Selected Viewport. Try both and note which one you prefer.
Open Edit > Editor Preferences, go to General, then Performance. Turn on Show Frame Rate and Memory, which shows these numbers in the editor at all times.

In the Editor Preferences, go to General, then Source Code, and find Source Code Editor. This is the program that Unreal opens when you want to read or write C++ code. Note what it is set to now. Change it only if you use a different program.

Open any project, or create one from the Third Person template. Open the Editor Preferences and go to Keyboard Shortcuts. Find the shortcut that toggles a breakpoint and the shortcut that starts Simulate.
Pick one command that you use often and rebind it, which means giving it a new key. Choose a key that you will remember.

Open any project, or create one from the Third Person template. Try each of these shortcuts in the editor: G switches game view on and off, Ctrl+B finds the selected asset in the Content Browser, Alt+drag makes a copy of an actor, H hides the selected actor and Ctrl+H shows hidden actors again, and F11 makes the viewport fullscreen.
Write which one of them you will use the most, and when you will use it.
